saints.name: Sts. Soter and Caius
saints.title: Popes and Martyrs
saints.shortBlurb: Two early popes sharing one feast, one famed for Rome's ancient charity, the other buried on the eve of the last persecution…
biography: Soter governed the Roman Church from about 166 to 174. St. Dionysius of Corinth, in a letter preserved by Eusebius, thanked him for upholding and increasing Rome's immemorial custom — 'the traditional custom of the Romans' — of sending alms to churches in every city and relief to the brethren labouring in the mines.

Dionysius adds that Soter's own letter was read aloud in the church of Corinth, like the earlier letter of Clement; it is now lost, though some have sought it in the so-called Second Epistle of Clement. A fifth-century writer credits Soter with a book against the Montanists, on uncertain authority.

Caius reigned twelve years, from 17 December 283 to 22 April 296, and was buried in the chapel of the popes in the cemetery of Callixtus. Later legend made him a kinsman of Diocletian and a martyr, but the fourth-century Depositio Episcoporum names him only among the bishops, for he died in the peace before the last persecution.

The two popes have shared a single commemoration on 22 April from the earliest martyrologies; in later centuries forged decretals were circulated under both their names — testimony to the weight their memory carried in the Roman Church.
saints.knownFor: Their governance of the early Roman Church and their witness to Christ.

sources.text: The Roman Martyrology (1914 English ed.; public domain), 22 April
